Thanks — I read through it and it's a good start. A lot of it matches what I picture. But before I sign off, there are some things I expected that either aren't here or are deliberately left out, and a few of them really matter to me.

The biggest one: when I save a link, I don't want to have to type the title and description myself every time. I'd expect that if I just paste in a web address, the app goes and grabs the page's name, a short description, and its little icon for me — I can tweak it after, but the point is I shouldn't have to do that work by hand. Right now it reads like I'm required to type the title, and the notes even say pulling that info automatically isn't part of this. That's a miss for me.

A few more things I assumed I'd have:

- A "read it later" idea. Sometimes I save something meaning to get to it, and I'd like to flag those and see just that list, then check them off once I've read them.
- Being able to tuck a bookmark away without deleting it — put it aside so it's out of my normal list, but I can still get it back later. Deleting feels too final for stuff I might still want.
- Sorting my list — at least by name or by when I added it. You've listed sorting as out of scope, but I'd want basic control over the order.
- Search that's a bit smarter than plain word matching — like searching an exact phrase, or combining a couple of tags to narrow things down.

And two I'd at least want us to talk about rather than rule out flat: keeping my own saved copy of a page so I don't lose it if the site disappears, and being able to bring in the bookmarks I already have (and get them back out).

I'm fine leaving out the collaboration, teams, and browser-extension stuff — that's not what I need right now.

Could you fold in the automatic title/description-grabbing, the read-later, the set-aside/archive, sorting, and the smarter search, and let me know your thinking on saved copies and importing? Then I'll be happy to look again.
